feedback: Pre-race review of the iteration 8 candidate. It keeps the iteration 6 design (narrow five-sensor array at x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03; sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2]; kp 2.0; kd 0.3; ki 0; last_direction) and changes one variable, base_speed from 1.1 to 1.2. Iteration 6 (kp 2.0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1) is the best raced design at 354.2, with 16 of 20 oval finishes. The speed evidence points the wrong way for an increase. At kp 2.5 and kd 0.3, base_speed 1.3 (iteration 1) gave 3 of 20 oval finishes and 1.25 oval line-loss events, while base_speed 1.1 (iteration 4) gave 11 of 20 and 0.95. Iteration 5 showed that 0.9 also hurt, so 1.1 is the only tested speed that works, and nothing so far shows a benefit above it. Iteration 7 showed that kd 0.25 alone cut oval completion to 1 of 20, so kd 0.3 stays. Each line-loss event costs about 15 points per unit progress, so a speed rise that adds line loss would cost more than the small time gain (the 60*(1 - t/3) term is worth about 20 points at the oval time of about 1.96 s). The candidate is valid and within contract limits, but its one change is the speed step that the earlier races argue against. Revise: restore base_speed to 1.1 and test kp alone at a smaller value. kp reduction from 2.5 to 2.0 cut oval line loss, max_error and s-bend line loss, so the same direction is the cleanest next test. If the race then shows line loss at or below iteration 6 levels, keep kp there and test base_speed 1.15 later, not 1.2 yet.
requested_changes: Set base_speed back to 1.1 and keep kd 0.3, ki 0, last_direction and the narrow geometry, since iteration 6 at 1.1 (354.2) is the best raced result and iteration 7 showed kd 0.25 drops oval completion to 1 of 20.

Change kp alone from 2.0 to 1.8. Iteration 4 to iteration 6 showed kp 2.5 to 2.0 cut oval line_loss_events from 0.95 to 0.85, max_error from 0.054 to 0.048, and s-bend line loss from 1.25 to 1.1, so further reduction is the next untested step in the same direction.

If kp 1.8 raises line_loss_events or max_error above the iteration 6 levels (0.85 and 0.048 on the oval), return to kp 2.0 and do not test speed above 1.1 until a speed step is supported by a line-loss result. Iteration 1 at 1.3 and iteration 4 at 1.1 show that the higher speed loses line.
